mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment rates above 7.5% indicate economic weakness that depresses corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 7.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When residential fixed investment (RSAFS) is high and the federal funds rate is low, it signals strong consumer demand and accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-recession recovery phase, a housing starts rate (HOUST) below 900,000 units signals weak residential demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during the post-recession recovery when HOUST is below 900,000, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor market (measured by nonfarm payrolls) indicates improving economic conditions that boost corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 235.0, it indicates elevated inflation that prompts monetary tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 235.0, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) both rise, it signals robust economic activity that supports corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic contraction, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.0 signals weakening manufacturing activity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle contraction when INDPRO declines below 98.0, or the Rank IC for the signal is negative over any 2-year rolling window.
